paragraphs: In Tanchuma, Vayera 8, R’ Yehudah HaLevi bar Shalom cites a teaching in his name. Hyman reports that the Old Tanchuma gives R’ Yehudah son of R’ Simon.

notes.text: The Old Tanchuma reading gives Yehudah son of Rabbi Simon. This short notice leaves the scope of the substitution implicit; it is not assigned to a specific place in the reporting chain.

The saved whole Buber1885 Tanchuma Vayera8:1 scalar has R’ Yehudah HaLevi ב״ר Shalom in R’ Yochanan [bar Nachman]’s name. The patronymic is bracketed there; this is a close parallel, not confirmation of Hyman’s reported Old Tanchuma Yehudah son of Simon variant. Hyman’s supplied18 remains alongside the comparison. Earlier standard18 nonmatch reports are finite research history, not a new whole-section inspection. These personal titles remain R' because the actual saved occurrences abbreviate them; scope of the substitution and Hyman’s edition remain held.

Hyman’s print (vol. II, pp. 570 and 683) cites Vayera 8. The supplied Hebrew here reads Vayera 18. In Buber’s Vayera 8, Yehudah HaLevi son of Shalom cites Yochanan [bar Nachman]. Buber’s note 62 gives the full patronymic from the Rome manuscript and reports that the printed text instead names Yehudah son of Rabbi Simon as the source of the teaching. The corresponding passage in the standard Tanchuma on Wikisource (Vayera 7) has that alternate attribution.
